name: Florida

agency.name: Division of Workers' Compensation, Florida Department of Financial Services

ttd.rateText: 66 2/3 or 66.67 percent of the average weekly wages during the continuance of disability (Fla. Stat. § 440.15(2)(a)); maximum = 100% of the statewide average weekly wage, adjusted to the nearest dollar (§ 440.12(2)).
ttd.minText: Not less than $20 per week; if wages at the time of injury are below $20 per week, the employee receives full weekly wages (Fla. Stat. § 440.12(2)).
ttd.periodLabel: injuries and illnesses occurring on or after January 1, 2026 (statewide AWW $1,357.95 for the four quarters ending June 30, 2025)

waiting.text: Compensation is not allowed for the first 7 days of disability, except medical benefits under s. 440.13; if the injury results in more than 21 days of disability, compensation is allowed from the commencement of the disability (Fla. Stat. § 440.12(1)).

ttdDuration.text: TTD may not exceed 104 weeks except as provided in the subsection, s. 440.12(1) and s. 440.14(3); benefits cease at the earlier of the maximum weeks or maximum medical improvement (Fla. Stat. § 440.15(2)(a)).

ppd.text: Impairment income benefits are paid biweekly at 75% of the employee's average weekly TTD benefit, based on a uniform permanent impairment rating schedule, starting the day after MMI or expiry of temporary benefits, for 3 weeks per percentage point of impairment as printed in the 2026 statute; reduced by 50% in weeks the employee earns at least the pre-injury AWW (Fla. Stat. § 440.15(3)(c)).

facts.text: Workers who lose an arm, leg, hand or foot, become paraplegic or quadriplegic, or lose sight in both eyes receive TTD at 80% of their average weekly wage rather than 66 2/3% (Fla. Stat. § 440.15(2)(b)).
The $20 weekly minimum has applied to every year in the Division's maximum compensation rate table, while the maximum rose from $1,295 (2025) to $1,358 (2026).

Only claimants with catastrophic injuries or who are incapable of employment are eligible for permanent total disability; if the accident occurs at age 70 or later, PTD is limited to 5 years after the PTD determination (Fla. Stat. § 440.15(1)).
Permanent impairment benefits for a psychiatric condition are limited to a 1-percent permanent impairment (Fla. Stat. § 440.15(3)(c)).
The maximum is reset each January 1 from the statewide average weekly wage that FloridaCommerce determines for the four quarters ending the previous June 30.

uncertain: Fla. Stat. § 440.15(3)(c) as displayed for 2026 reads '3 weeks for each percentage point of impairment'; earlier versions used a tiered schedule (2/3/4/6 weeks). Verify against the 2026 session law before using a tiered formula.
